conversation.content: I'm exploring Specialty Nursing Neonatal Bachelor of Science in Nursing. Please keep that as our subject.

I’ll keep **Specialty Nursing (Neonatal), Bachelor of Science in Nursing, Part-time** as our subject.

It is an active **60-credit**, fully online BCIT Bachelor of Science in Nursing program. Its neonatal curriculum includes courses such as **NSNE 7100 – Neonatal Theory 1**, **NSNE 7300 – Neonatal Clinical 1**, and **NSNE 7900 – Clinical Preceptorship in Neonatal Nursing**, alongside core/management, Liberal Studies, and approved electives.

[View the BCIT program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
Give me a short overview.

The program combines neonatal specialty training with broader nursing leadership, inquiry, management, and Liberal Studies. Its curriculum includes:

- **21 credits** of required neonatal courses
- At least **3 credits** from an approved neonatal elective pool
- **24 credits** in the Core/Management component
- **12 credits** in Liberal Studies

Entrance requirements include English Studies 12 at 73% or equivalent, a nursing diploma, current practising RN registration, and at least six months of acute-care experience. Clinical participation also requires confirmation of items such as current CPR certification and respirator fit testing.

[View the BCIT program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
What credential does it lead to?

It leads to a **Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BScN)** credential. [View the BCIT program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
Where would I study?

You would study **fully online** through BCIT. [View the program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
Is it online or in person?
It is delivered **fully online**. [View the BCIT program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)

rule_sets.name: Specialty Nursing entrance requirements
rule_sets.notes: About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* Domestic students: January 2nd* International students: November 1st* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* Domestic students: April 1st* International students: February 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* Domestic students: September 1st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements The following are requirements for entry into Specialty Nursing certificate and degree courses. Enforcement or waiving of any or all entry requirements is at the discretion of the program head. If you have any questions about your experience or qualifications, please contact the program head. English language proficiency: Category 1 – English Studies 12 (73%) or equivalent Post-secondary education: diploma in nursing Current practicing registration with one of the following: BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) or Canadian provincial equivalent or Registered Nurse (RN) license number (if practicing outside Canada) Work Experience: minimum six months work experience in an acute care setting Submit a resume of work experience with your application. Exceptions may be granted for undergraduate students taking entry-level theory courses or new graduates. A resume is required for placement in the program. If you have questions about whether your work experience qualifies, please contact the program head. Interested nurses from international practice, residential, or other areas of care lacking recent (within two years) acute care experience may be required to complete a refresher course. BCIT recommends the following programs: Douglas College Kwantlen Polytechnic University Thompson Rivers University Please contact one of the institutions above, as well as the program head, to determine an appropriate preparatory course of study. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Clinical requirements Note: Effective immediately, all healthcare workers who come into contact with patients at publicly funded healthcare facilities or in the community, including at long-term care facilities, will have to get the influenza vaccine or wear a mask during flu season. This policy affects all students who will be entering a clinical setting. As such, you will be required to provide proof of your immunization or agree to wear a mask at all times prior to being placed in your clinical studies. Basic Cardiac Life Support Certification All students participating in clinical courses must have current Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), Level C or Level Health Care Provider (HCP). CPR certification must be from a Canadian provider and include a practical component. The original certificate must be presented upon application to clinical courses. BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) registration As well as providing this information at the time of admission, BCIT requires students to provide proof of BCCNM membership, Canadian provincial equivalent, or RN license number for each clinical course. Without proper registration, you will not be permitted to continue in the course. Face Respirator Fit Testing A face piece respiratory fit test is required before students are permitted to enter the clinical practicum. Upon successful completion of the fit test, the original certificate must be presented to the program and annual re-fitting is required. Students are expected to carry their certificate with them at all times during their practicum. For the Respirator Fit Testing, fit testing with a N95 respirator (1860, 1860s, or 1870) is required and must be performed, in accordance with CSA Standard CAN/CSA-Z94.4-02. Fit Testing must also include inspection, cleaning, maintenance, and storage of protective equipment. Students will be given specific instructions in preparation for their fit testing by the provider they choose. International applicants This program is available to international applicants who will complete the program from outside Canada or who currently have a valid work permit in Canada that will be valid for the duration of clinical training. Study permit: International applicants accepted into this program are not eligible for a study permit. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : While this program currently meets the study program - graduates with a bachelor’s degree criteria to apply for a PGWP, this program is not eligible for a PGWP due to other criteria not being met. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a bachelor’s degree. Apply to program International students must receive program head approval before applying. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply Prior Learning Assessment & Recognition (PLAR) The program faculty assesses learners with previous Specialty Nursing course work and relevant work experience on an individual basis. The program assesses learners with previous BCIT course work for potential credit into the degree program. The program may grant transfer of credit for non-BCIT Specialty courses. The program assesses experiential learning through prior learning assessment processes. The Registrar's office assesses transfer of credit for Liberal Studies courses. BCIT requires original, sealed transcripts and course outlines to assess transfer of credit. myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. rule_sets.notes: Graduate employment outcomes The BCIT student outcomes report presents summary findings from the annual survey of former students administered by BC Stats one to two years after graduation. These reports combine the last three years of available results for the 2023-2025 BCIT Outcomes Surveys of 2022-2024 graduates and for Degree 2021-2023 graduates. The reports are organized into three-page summaries containing information on graduates’ labour market experiences and opinions regarding their education. More detailed information can be accessed at the BC Student Outcomes website. To view these results, you may need to have the Adobe Acrobat Reader installed in your Web browser. request.question: What should I know before applying?

conversation.content: Give me a short overview.

The program combines neonatal specialty training with broader nursing leadership, inquiry, management, and Liberal Studies. Its curriculum includes:

- **21 credits** of required neonatal courses
- At least **3 credits** from an approved neonatal elective pool
- **24 credits** in the Core/Management component
- **12 credits** in Liberal Studies

rule_sets.name: Specialty Nursing entrance requirements
rule_sets.notes: About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* Domestic students: January 2nd* International students: November 1st* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* Domestic students: April 1st* International students: February 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* Domestic students: September 1st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements The following are requirements for entry into Specialty Nursing certificate and degree courses. Enforcement or waiving of any or all entry requirements is at the discretion of the program head. If you have any questions about your experience or qualifications, please contact the program head. English language proficiency: Category 1 – English Studies 12 (73%) or equivalent Post-secondary education: diploma in nursing Current practicing registration with one of the following: BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) or Canadian provincial equivalent or Registered Nurse (RN) license number (if practicing outside Canada) Work Experience: minimum six months work experience in an acute care setting Submit a resume of work experience with your application. Exceptions may be granted for undergraduate students taking entry-level theory courses or new graduates. A resume is required for placement in the program. If you have questions about whether your work experience qualifies, please contact the program head. Interested nurses from international practice, residential, or other areas of care lacking recent (within two years) acute care experience may be required to complete a refresher course. BCIT recommends the following programs: Douglas College Kwantlen Polytechnic University Thompson Rivers University Please contact one of the institutions above, as well as the program head, to determine an appropriate preparatory course of study. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Clinical requirements Note: Effective immediately, all healthcare workers who come into contact with patients at publicly funded healthcare facilities or in the community, including at long-term care facilities, will have to get the influenza vaccine or wear a mask during flu season. This policy affects all students who will be entering a clinical setting. As such, you will be required to provide proof of your immunization or agree to wear a mask at all times prior to being placed in your clinical studies. Basic Cardiac Life Support Certification All students participating in clinical courses must have current Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), Level C or Level Health Care Provider (HCP). CPR certification must be from a Canadian provider and include a practical component. The original certificate must be presented upon application to clinical courses. BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) registration As well as providing this information at the time of admission, BCIT requires students to provide proof of BCCNM membership, Canadian provincial equivalent, or RN license number for each clinical course. Without proper registration, you will not be permitted to continue in the course. Face Respirator Fit Testing A face piece respiratory fit test is required before students are permitted to enter the clinical practicum. Upon successful completion of the fit test, the original certificate must be presented to the program and annual re-fitting is required. Students are expected to carry their certificate with them at all times during their practicum. For the Respirator Fit Testing, fit testing with a N95 respirator (1860, 1860s, or 1870) is required and must be performed, in accordance with CSA Standard CAN/CSA-Z94.4-02. Fit Testing must also include inspection, cleaning, maintenance, and storage of protective equipment. Students will be given specific instructions in preparation for their fit testing by the provider they choose. International applicants This program is available to international applicants who will complete the program from outside Canada or who currently have a valid work permit in Canada that will be valid for the duration of clinical training. Study permit: International applicants accepted into this program are not eligible for a study permit. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : While this program currently meets the study program - graduates with a bachelor’s degree criteria to apply for a PGWP, this program is not eligible for a PGWP due to other criteria not being met. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a bachelor’s degree. Apply to program International students must receive program head approval before applying. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply Prior Learning Assessment & Recognition (PLAR) The program faculty assesses learners with previous Specialty Nursing course work and relevant work experience on an individual basis. The program assesses learners with previous BCIT course work for potential credit into the degree program. The program may grant transfer of credit for non-BCIT Specialty courses. The program assesses experiential learning through prior learning assessment processes. The Registrar's office assesses transfer of credit for Liberal Studies courses. BCIT requires original, sealed transcripts and course outlines to assess transfer of credit. myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. Go back Overview Next up Costs & Supplies

Entrance requirements The following are requirements for entry into Specialty Nursing certificate and degree courses. English language proficiency: Category 1 \u2013 English Studies 12 (73%) or equivalent Post-secondary education: diploma in nursing Current practicing registration with one of the following: BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) or Canadian provincial equivalent or Registered Nurse (RN) license number (if practicing outside Canada) Work Experience: minimum six months work experience in an acute care setting Submit a resume of work experience with your application. Exceptions may be granted for undergraduate students taking entry-level theory courses or new graduates. A resume is required for placement in the program. If you have questions about whether your work experience qualifies, please contact the program head. Interested nurses from international practice, residential, or other areas of care lacking recent (within two years) acute care experience may be required to complete a refresher course. BCIT recommends the following programs: Douglas College Kwantlen Polytechnic University Thompson Rivers University Please contact one of the institutions above, as well as the program head, to determine an appropriate preparatory course of study. Read more about how to meet BCIT\u2019s entrance requirements Clinical requirements Note: Effective immediately, all healthcare workers who come into contact with patients at publicly funded healthcare facilities or in the community, including at long-term care facilities, will have to get the influenza vaccine or wear a mask during flu season. This policy affects all students who will be entering a clinical setting. As such, you will be required to provide proof of your immunization or agree to wear a mask at all times prior to being placed in your clinical studies. Basic Cardiac Life Support Certification All students participating in clinical courses must have current Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), Level C or Level Health Care Provider (HCP). CPR certification must be from a Canadian provider and include a practical component. The original certificate must be presented upon application to clinical courses. BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) registration As well as providing this information at the time of admission, BCIT requires students to provide proof of BCCNM membership, Canadian provincial equivalent, or RN license number for each clinical course. Without proper registration, you will not be permitted to continue in the course. Face Respirator Fit Testing A face piece respiratory fit test is required before students are permitted to enter the clinical practicum. Upon successful completion of the fit test, the original certificate must be presented to the program and annual re-fitting is required. Students are expected to carry their certificate with them at all times during their practicum. For the Respirator Fit Testing, fit testing with a N95 respirator (1860, 1860s, or 1870) is required and must be performed, in accordance with CSA Standard CAN/CSA-Z94.4-02. Fit Testing must also include inspection, cleaning, maintenance, and storage of protective equipment. Students will be given specific instructions in preparation for their fit testing by the provider they choose. International applicants This program is available to international applicants who will complete the program from outside Canada or who currently have a valid work permit in Canada that will be valid for the duration of clinical training. Study permit: International applicants accepted into this program are not eligible for a study permit. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : While this program currently meets the study program - graduates with a bachelor\u2019s degree criteria to apply for a PGWP, this program is not eligible for a PGWP due to other criteria not being met. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a bachelor\u2019s degree. Apply to program International students must receive program head approval before applying. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply Prior Learning Assessment & Recognition (PLAR) The program faculty assesses learners with previous Specialty Nursing course work and relevant work experience on an individual basis. The program assesses learners with previous BCIT course work for potential credit into the degree program. The program may grant transfer of credit for non-BCIT Specialty courses. The program assesses experiential learning through prior learning assessment processes. The Registrar's office assesses transfer of credit for Liberal Studies courses. BCIT requires original, sealed transcripts and course outlines to assess transfer of credit. myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. content.text:
Before applying, check these points:

- **Still to establish:** English Studies 12 at **73% or equivalent**, a post-secondary nursing diploma, and at least **six months of acute-care experience**.
- **Requires BCIT confirmation:** current practising RN registration and your résumé/work-experience documentation. The program head has discretion over exceptions and whether experience qualifies.
- **Clinical readiness:** clinical participation later requires verified RN registration, qualifying current CPR certification, respirator fit testing, and compliance with the influenza immunization or masking policy.

Applications are accepted throughout the year for January, April, and September intakes, but an intake may fill early. International applicants need program-head approval before applying and must study from outside Canada or hold a work permit valid through clinical training; the program is not eligible for a study permit or PGWP.

Your best next step is to confirm your acute-care experience and registration status with the program head before submitting an application.

[View application and program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)

response.answer:
International applicants may apply if they either:

- complete the program from outside Canada, or
- hold a Canadian work permit valid for the full duration of clinical training.

You must receive **program-head approval before applying**. The regular entrance requirements still apply, including the nursing diploma, English requirement, RN registration, and acute-care experience; none can be assessed without your background details. Registration, experience equivalency, and clinical documentation require BCIT confirmation.

This program is **not eligible for a study permit or a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)**.

[View BCIT’s international applicant details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)

rule_sets.name: Specialty Nursing entrance requirements
rule_sets.notes: About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* Domestic students: January 2nd* International students: November 1st* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* Domestic students: April 1st* International students: February 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* Domestic students: September 1st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements The following are requirements for entry into Specialty Nursing certificate and degree courses. Enforcement or waiving of any or all entry requirements is at the discretion of the program head. If you have any questions about your experience or qualifications, please contact the program head. English language proficiency: Category 1 – English Studies 12 (73%) or equivalent Post-secondary education: diploma in nursing Current practicing registration with one of the following: BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) or Canadian provincial equivalent or Registered Nurse (RN) license number (if practicing outside Canada) Work Experience: minimum six months work experience in an acute care setting Submit a resume of work experience with your application. Exceptions may be granted for undergraduate students taking entry-level theory courses or new graduates. A resume is required for placement in the program. If you have questions about whether your work experience qualifies, please contact the program head. Interested nurses from international practice, residential, or other areas of care lacking recent (within two years) acute care experience may be required to complete a refresher course. BCIT recommends the following programs: Douglas College Kwantlen Polytechnic University Thompson Rivers University Please contact one of the institutions above, as well as the program head, to determine an appropriate preparatory course of study. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Clinical requirements Note: Effective immediately, all healthcare workers who come into contact with patients at publicly funded healthcare facilities or in the community, including at long-term care facilities, will have to get the influenza vaccine or wear a mask during flu season. This policy affects all students who will be entering a clinical setting. As such, you will be required to provide proof of your immunization or agree to wear a mask at all times prior to being placed in your clinical studies. Basic Cardiac Life Support Certification All students participating in clinical courses must have current Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), Level C or Level Health Care Provider (HCP). CPR certification must be from a Canadian provider and include a practical component. The original certificate must be presented upon application to clinical courses. BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) registration As well as providing this information at the time of admission, BCIT requires students to provide proof of BCCNM membership, Canadian provincial equivalent, or RN license number for each clinical course. Without proper registration, you will not be permitted to continue in the course. Face Respirator Fit Testing A face piece respiratory fit test is required before students are permitted to enter the clinical practicum. Upon successful completion of the fit test, the original certificate must be presented to the program and annual re-fitting is required. Students are expected to carry their certificate with them at all times during their practicum. For the Respirator Fit Testing, fit testing with a N95 respirator (1860, 1860s, or 1870) is required and must be performed, in accordance with CSA Standard CAN/CSA-Z94.4-02. Fit Testing must also include inspection, cleaning, maintenance, and storage of protective equipment. Students will be given specific instructions in preparation for their fit testing by the provider they choose. International applicants This program is available to international applicants who will complete the program from outside Canada or who currently have a valid work permit in Canada that will be valid for the duration of clinical training. Study permit: International applicants accepted into this program are not eligible for a study permit. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : While this program currently meets the study program - graduates with a bachelor’s degree criteria to apply for a PGWP, this program is not eligible for a PGWP due to other criteria not being met. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a bachelor’s degree. Apply to program International students must receive program head approval before applying. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply Prior Learning Assessment & Recognition (PLAR) The program faculty assesses learners with previous Specialty Nursing course work and relevant work experience on an individual basis. The program assesses learners with previous BCIT course work for potential credit into the degree program. The program may grant transfer of credit for non-BCIT Specialty courses. The program assesses experiential learning through prior learning assessment processes. The Registrar's office assesses transfer of credit for Liberal Studies courses. BCIT requires original, sealed transcripts and course outlines to assess transfer of credit. myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. Go back Overview Next up Costs & Supplies

Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* Domestic students: January 2nd* International students: November 1st* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* Domestic students: April 1st* International students: February 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* Domestic students: September 1st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements The following are requirements for entry into Specialty Nursing certificate and degree courses. Enforcement or waiving of any or all entry requirements is at the discretion of the program head. If you have any questions about your experience or qualifications, please contact the program head. English language proficiency: Category 1 \u2013 English Studies 12 (73%) or equivalent Post-secondary education: diploma in nursing Current practicing registration with one of the following: BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) or Canadian provincial equivalent or Registered Nurse (RN) license number (if practicing outside Canada) Work Experience: minimum six months work experience in an acute care setting Submit a resume of work experience with your application. Exceptions may be granted for undergraduate students taking entry-level theory courses or new graduates. A resume is required for placement in the program. If you have questions about whether your work experience qualifies, please contact the program head. Interested nurses from international practice, residential, or other areas of care lacking recent (within two years) acute care experience may be required to complete a refresher course. BCIT recommends the following programs: Douglas College Kwantlen Polytechnic University Thompson Rivers University Please contact one of the institutions above, as well as the program head, to determine an appropriate preparatory course of study. Read more about how to meet BCIT\u2019s entrance requirements Clinical requirements Note: Effective immediately, all healthcare workers who come into contact with patients at publicly funded healthcare facilities or in the community, including at long-term care facilities, will have to get the influenza vaccine or wear a mask during flu season. This policy affects all students who will be entering a clinical setting. As such, you will be required to provide proof of your immunization or agree to wear a mask at all times prior to being placed in your clinical studies. Basic Cardiac Life Support Certification All students participating in clinical courses must have current Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), Level C or Level Health Care Provider (HCP). CPR certification must be from a Canadian provider and include a practical component. The original certificate must be presented upon application to clinical courses. BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) registration As well as providing this information at the time of admission, BCIT requires students to provide proof of BCCNM membership, Canadian provincial equivalent, or RN license number for each clinical course. Without proper registration, you will not be permitted to continue in the course. Face Respirator Fit Testing A face piece respiratory fit test is required before students are permitted to enter the clinical practicum. Upon successful completion of the fit test, the original certificate must be presented to the program and annual re-fitting is required. Students are expected to carry their certificate with them at all times during their practicum. For the Respirator Fit Testing, fit testing with a N95 respirator (1860, 1860s, or 1870) is required and must be performed, in accordance with CSA Standard CAN/CSA-Z94.4-02. Fit Testing must also include inspection, cleaning, maintenance, and storage of protective equipment. Students will be given specific instructions in preparation for their fit testing by the provider they choose. International applicants This program is available to international applicants who will complete the program from outside Canada or who currently have a valid work permit in Canada that will be valid for the duration of clinical training. Study permit: International applicants accepted into this program are not eligible for a study permit. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : While this program currently meets the study program - graduates with a bachelor\u2019s degree criteria to apply for a PGWP, this program is not eligible for a PGWP due to other criteria not being met. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a bachelor\u2019s degree. Apply to program International students must receive program head approval before applying. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply Prior Learning Assessment & Recognition (PLAR) The program faculty assesses learners with previous Specialty Nursing course work and relevant work experience on an individual basis. The program assesses learners with previous BCIT course work for potential credit into the degree program. The program may grant transfer of credit for non-BCIT Specialty courses. The program assesses experiential learning through prior learning assessment processes. The Registrar's office assesses transfer of credit for Liberal Studies courses. BCIT requires original, sealed transcripts and course outlines to assess transfer of credit. myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. content.text:
International applicants may apply if they either:

- complete the program from outside Canada, or
- hold a Canadian work permit valid for the full duration of clinical training.

You must receive **program-head approval before applying**. The regular entrance requirements still apply, including the nursing diploma, English requirement, RN registration, and acute-care experience; none can be assessed without your background details. Registration, experience equivalency, and clinical documentation require BCIT confirmation.

This program is **not eligible for a study permit or a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)**.

[View BCIT’s international applicant details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)

conversation.content: Where would I study?

You would study **fully online** through BCIT. [View the program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
Is it online or in person?
It is delivered **fully online**. [View the BCIT program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
Is it full-time or part-time?
It is a **part-time** program. [View the BCIT program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
What should I know before applying?

Before applying, check these points:

- **Still to establish:** English Studies 12 at **73% or equivalent**, a post-secondary nursing diploma, and at least **six months of acute-care experience**.
- **Requires BCIT confirmation:** current practising RN registration and your résumé/work-experience documentation. The program head has discretion over exceptions and whether experience qualifies.
- **Clinical readiness:** clinical participation later requires verified RN registration, qualifying current CPR certification, respirator fit testing, and compliance with the influenza immunization or masking policy.

Applications are accepted throughout the year for January, April, and September intakes, but an intake may fill early. International applicants need program-head approval before applying and must study from outside Canada or hold a work permit valid through clinical training; the program is not eligible for a study permit or PGWP.

Your best next step is to confirm your acute-care experience and registration status with the program head before submitting an application.

expectation.question: Does that guarantee admission?

response.answer:
No. Meeting the entrance requirements does **not guarantee admission**. The program head may assess or waive requirements at their discretion, and an intake may fill before the deadline.

Your most useful next step is to confirm your RN registration and acute-care experience with the program head, then apply early.

[View BCIT program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.

rule_sets.name: Specialty Nursing entrance requirements
rule_sets.notes: About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* Domestic students: January 2nd* International students: November 1st* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* Domestic students: April 1st* International students: February 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* Domestic students: September 1st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements The following are requirements for entry into Specialty Nursing certificate and degree courses. Enforcement or waiving of any or all entry requirements is at the discretion of the program head. If you have any questions about your experience or qualifications, please contact the program head. English language proficiency: Category 1 – English Studies 12 (73%) or equivalent Post-secondary education: diploma in nursing Current practicing registration with one of the following: BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) or Canadian provincial equivalent or Registered Nurse (RN) license number (if practicing outside Canada) Work Experience: minimum six months work experience in an acute care setting Submit a resume of work experience with your application. Exceptions may be granted for undergraduate students taking entry-level theory courses or new graduates. A resume is required for placement in the program. If you have questions about whether your work experience qualifies, please contact the program head. Interested nurses from international practice, residential, or other areas of care lacking recent (within two years) acute care experience may be required to complete a refresher course. BCIT recommends the following programs: Douglas College Kwantlen Polytechnic University Thompson Rivers University Please contact one of the institutions above, as well as the program head, to determine an appropriate preparatory course of study. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Clinical requirements Note: Effective immediately, all healthcare workers who come into contact with patients at publicly funded healthcare facilities or in the community, including at long-term care facilities, will have to get the influenza vaccine or wear a mask during flu season. This policy affects all students who will be entering a clinical setting. As such, you will be required to provide proof of your immunization or agree to wear a mask at all times prior to being placed in your clinical studies. Basic Cardiac Life Support Certification All students participating in clinical courses must have current Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), Level C or Level Health Care Provider (HCP). CPR certification must be from a Canadian provider and include a practical component. The original certificate must be presented upon application to clinical courses. BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) registration As well as providing this information at the time of admission, BCIT requires students to provide proof of BCCNM membership, Canadian provincial equivalent, or RN license number for each clinical course. Without proper registration, you will not be permitted to continue in the course. Face Respirator Fit Testing A face piece respiratory fit test is required before students are permitted to enter the clinical practicum. Upon successful completion of the fit test, the original certificate must be presented to the program and annual re-fitting is required. Students are expected to carry their certificate with them at all times during their practicum. For the Respirator Fit Testing, fit testing with a N95 respirator (1860, 1860s, or 1870) is required and must be performed, in accordance with CSA Standard CAN/CSA-Z94.4-02. Fit Testing must also include inspection, cleaning, maintenance, and storage of protective equipment. Students will be given specific instructions in preparation for their fit testing by the provider they choose. International applicants This program is available to international applicants who will complete the program from outside Canada or who currently have a valid work permit in Canada that will be valid for the duration of clinical training. Study permit: International applicants accepted into this program are not eligible for a study permit. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : While this program currently meets the study program - graduates with a bachelor’s degree criteria to apply for a PGWP, this program is not eligible for a PGWP due to other criteria not being met. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a bachelor’s degree. Apply to program International students must receive program head approval before applying. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply Prior Learning Assessment & Recognition (PLAR) The program faculty assesses learners with previous Specialty Nursing course work and relevant work experience on an individual basis. The program assesses learners with previous BCIT course work for potential credit into the degree program. The program may grant transfer of credit for non-BCIT Specialty courses. The program assesses experiential learning through prior learning assessment processes. The Registrar's office assesses transfer of credit for Liberal Studies courses. BCIT requires original, sealed transcripts and course outlines to assess transfer of credit. myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. request.question: Which details need human confirmation?

conversation.content: Is it online or in person?
It is delivered **fully online**. [View the BCIT program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
Is it full-time or part-time?
It is a **part-time** program. [View the BCIT program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
What should I know before applying?

Before applying, check these points:

- **Still to establish:** English Studies 12 at **73% or equivalent**, a post-secondary nursing diploma, and at least **six months of acute-care experience**.
- **Requires BCIT confirmation:** current practising RN registration and your résumé/work-experience documentation. The program head has discretion over exceptions and whether experience qualifies.
- **Clinical readiness:** clinical participation later requires verified RN registration, qualifying current CPR certification, respirator fit testing, and compliance with the influenza immunization or masking policy.

Applications are accepted throughout the year for January, April, and September intakes, but an intake may fill early. International applicants need program-head approval before applying and must study from outside Canada or hold a work permit valid through clinical training; the program is not eligible for a study permit or PGWP.

Your best next step is to confirm your acute-care experience and registration status with the program head before submitting an application.

[View application and program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
What about international applicants?

International applicants may apply if they either:

- complete the program from outside Canada, or
- hold a Canadian work permit valid for the full duration of clinical training.

You must receive **program-head approval before applying**. The regular entrance requirements still apply, including the nursing diploma, English requirement, RN registration, and acute-care experience; none can be assessed without your background details. Registration, experience equivalency, and clinical documentation require BCIT confirmation.

This program is **not eligible for a study permit or a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)**.

[View BCIT’s international applicant details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
Does that guarantee admission?

No. Meeting the entrance requirements does **not guarantee admission**. The program head may assess or waive requirements at their discretion, and an intake may fill before the deadline.

Your most useful next step is to confirm your RN registration and acute-care experience with the program head, then apply early.

[View BCIT program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.

- **Current practising RN registration**
- Whether your **acute-care experience is recent, relevant, or equivalent**, including any exception or refresher-course need
- Your **résumé and work-experience documentation**
- For international applicants, **program-head approval before applying**
- Before clinical participation: valid **RN registration, qualifying CPR certification, respirator fit testing**, and compliance with the **influenza immunization or masking policy**
- The required total **clinical-practice hours**, because no numeric threshold is published in the program record

[View the program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)

User: Is it online or in person?
Assistant: It is delivered **fully online**. [View the BCIT program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
User: Is it full-time or part-time?

User: What should I know before applying?
Assistant: Before applying, check these points:

- **Still to establish:** English Studies 12 at **73% or equivalent**, a post-secondary nursing diploma, and at least **six months of acute-care experience**.
- **Requires BCIT confirmation:** current practising RN registration and your résumé/work-experience documentation. The program head has discretion over exceptions and whether experience qualifies.
- **Clinical readiness:** clinical participation later requires verified RN registration, qualifying current CPR certification, respirator fit testing, and compliance with the influenza immunization or masking policy.

- complete the program from outside Canada, or
- hold a Canadian work permit valid for the full duration of clinical training.

rule_sets.name: Specialty Nursing entrance requirements
rule_sets.notes: About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* Domestic students: January 2nd* International students: November 1st* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* Domestic students: April 1st* International students: February 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* Domestic students: September 1st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements The following are requirements for entry into Specialty Nursing certificate and degree courses. Enforcement or waiving of any or all entry requirements is at the discretion of the program head. If you have any questions about your experience or qualifications, please contact the program head. English language proficiency: Category 1 – English Studies 12 (73%) or equivalent Post-secondary education: diploma in nursing Current practicing registration with one of the following: BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) or Canadian provincial equivalent or Registered Nurse (RN) license number (if practicing outside Canada) Work Experience: minimum six months work experience in an acute care setting Submit a resume of work experience with your application. Exceptions may be granted for undergraduate students taking entry-level theory courses or new graduates. A resume is required for placement in the program. If you have questions about whether your work experience qualifies, please contact the program head. Interested nurses from international practice, residential, or other areas of care lacking recent (within two years) acute care experience may be required to complete a refresher course. BCIT recommends the following programs: Douglas College Kwantlen Polytechnic University Thompson Rivers University Please contact one of the institutions above, as well as the program head, to determine an appropriate preparatory course of study. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Clinical requirements Note: Effective immediately, all healthcare workers who come into contact with patients at publicly funded healthcare facilities or in the community, including at long-term care facilities, will have to get the influenza vaccine or wear a mask during flu season. This policy affects all students who will be entering a clinical setting. As such, you will be required to provide proof of your immunization or agree to wear a mask at all times prior to being placed in your clinical studies. Basic Cardiac Life Support Certification All students participating in clinical courses must have current Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), Level C or Level Health Care Provider (HCP). CPR certification must be from a Canadian provider and include a practical component. The original certificate must be presented upon application to clinical courses. BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) registration As well as providing this information at the time of admission, BCIT requires students to provide proof of BCCNM membership, Canadian provincial equivalent, or RN license number for each clinical course. Without proper registration, you will not be permitted to continue in the course. Face Respirator Fit Testing A face piece respiratory fit test is required before students are permitted to enter the clinical practicum. Upon successful completion of the fit test, the original certificate must be presented to the program and annual re-fitting is required. Students are expected to carry their certificate with them at all times during their practicum. For the Respirator Fit Testing, fit testing with a N95 respirator (1860, 1860s, or 1870) is required and must be performed, in accordance with CSA Standard CAN/CSA-Z94.4-02. Fit Testing must also include inspection, cleaning, maintenance, and storage of protective equipment. Students will be given specific instructions in preparation for their fit testing by the provider they choose. International applicants This program is available to international applicants who will complete the program from outside Canada or who currently have a valid work permit in Canada that will be valid for the duration of clinical training. Study permit: International applicants accepted into this program are not eligible for a study permit. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : While this program currently meets the study program - graduates with a bachelor’s degree criteria to apply for a PGWP, this program is not eligible for a PGWP due to other criteria not being met. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a bachelor’s degree. Apply to program International students must receive program head approval before applying. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply Prior Learning Assessment & Recognition (PLAR) The program faculty assesses learners with previous Specialty Nursing course work and relevant work experience on an individual basis. The program assesses learners with previous BCIT course work for potential credit into the degree program. The program may grant transfer of credit for non-BCIT Specialty courses. The program assesses experiential learning through prior learning assessment processes. The Registrar's office assesses transfer of credit for Liberal Studies courses. BCIT requires original, sealed transcripts and course outlines to assess transfer of credit. myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. Go back Overview Next up Costs & Supplies

conversation.content: Is it full-time or part-time?
It is a **part-time** program. [View the BCIT program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
What should I know before applying?

Before applying, check these points:

- **Still to establish:** English Studies 12 at **73% or equivalent**, a post-secondary nursing diploma, and at least **six months of acute-care experience**.
- **Requires BCIT confirmation:** current practising RN registration and your résumé/work-experience documentation. The program head has discretion over exceptions and whether experience qualifies.
- **Clinical readiness:** clinical participation later requires verified RN registration, qualifying current CPR certification, respirator fit testing, and compliance with the influenza immunization or masking policy.

Applications are accepted throughout the year for January, April, and September intakes, but an intake may fill early. International applicants need program-head approval before applying and must study from outside Canada or hold a work permit valid through clinical training; the program is not eligible for a study permit or PGWP.

Your best next step is to confirm your acute-care experience and registration status with the program head before submitting an application.

[View application and program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
What about international applicants?

International applicants may apply if they either:

- complete the program from outside Canada, or
- hold a Canadian work permit valid for the full duration of clinical training.

You must receive **program-head approval before applying**. The regular entrance requirements still apply, including the nursing diploma, English requirement, RN registration, and acute-care experience; none can be assessed without your background details. Registration, experience equivalency, and clinical documentation require BCIT confirmation.

This program is **not eligible for a study permit or a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)**.

[View BCIT’s international applicant details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
Does that guarantee admission?

No. Meeting the entrance requirements does **not guarantee admission**. The program head may assess or waive requirements at their discretion, and an intake may fill before the deadline.

Your most useful next step is to confirm your RN registration and acute-care experience with the program head, then apply early.

[View BCIT program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.
Which details need human confirmation?

Human confirmation is needed for:

- **Current practising RN registration**
- Whether your **acute-care experience is recent, relevant, or equivalent**, including any exception or refresher-course need
- Your **résumé and work-experience documentation**
- For international applicants, **program-head approval before applying**
- Before clinical participation: valid **RN registration, qualifying CPR certification, respirator fit testing**, and compliance with the **influenza immunization or masking policy**
- The required total **clinical-practice hours**, because no numeric threshold is published in the program record

[View the program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)

Recent conversation:
User: Is it full-time or part-time?
Assistant: It is a **part-time** program. [View the BCIT program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
User: What should I know before applying?
Assistant: Before applying, check these points:

- **Still to establish:** English Studies 12 at **73% or equivalent**, a post-secondary nursing diploma, and at least **six months of acute-care experience**.
- **Requires BCIT confirmation:** current practising RN registration and your résumé/work-experience documentation. The program head has discretion over exceptions and whether experience qualifies.
- **Clinical readiness:** clinical participation later requires verified RN registration, qualifying current CPR certification, respirator fit testing, and compliance with the influenza immunization or masking policy.

Applications are accepted throughout the year for January, April, and September intakes, but an intake may fill early. International applicants need program-head approval before applying and must study from outside Canada or hold a work permit valid through clinical training; the program is not eligible for a study permit or PGWP.

Your best next step is to confirm your acute-care experience and registration status with the program head before submitting an application.

[View application and program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
User: What about international applicants?
Assistant: International applicants may apply if they either:

- complete the program from outside Canada, or
- hold a Canadian work permit valid for the full duration of clinical training.

You must receive **program-head approval before applying**. The regular entrance requirements still apply, including the nursing diploma, English requirement, RN registration, and acute-care experience; none can be assessed without your background details. Registration, experience equivalency, and clinical documentation require BCIT confirmation.

This program is **not eligible for a study permit or a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)**.

[View BCIT’s international applicant details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)
User: Does that guarantee admission?
Assistant: No. Meeting the entrance requirements does **not guarantee admission**. The program head may assess or waive requirements at their discretion, and an intake may fill before the deadline.

Your most useful next step is to confirm your RN registration and acute-care experience with the program head, then apply early.

[View BCIT program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.
User: Which details need human confirmation?
Assistant: Human confirmation is needed for:

- **Current practising RN registration**
- Whether your **acute-care experience is recent, relevant, or equivalent**, including any exception or refresher-course need
- Your **résumé and work-experience documentation**
- For international applicants, **program-head approval before applying**
- Before clinical participation: valid **RN registration, qualifying CPR certification, respirator fit testing**, and compliance with the **influenza immunization or masking policy**
- The required total **clinical-practice hours**, because no numeric threshold is published in the program record

[View the program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/specialty-nursing-neonatal-bachelor-of-science-in-nursing-part-time-distance-and-online-learning-810cbsn/)

rule_sets.name: Specialty Nursing entrance requirements
rule_sets.notes: About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* Domestic students: January 2nd* International students: November 1st* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* Domestic students: April 1st* International students: February 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* Domestic students: September 1st* International students: July 2nd* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements The following are requirements for entry into Specialty Nursing certificate and degree courses. Enforcement or waiving of any or all entry requirements is at the discretion of the program head. If you have any questions about your experience or qualifications, please contact the program head. English language proficiency: Category 1 – English Studies 12 (73%) or equivalent Post-secondary education: diploma in nursing Current practicing registration with one of the following: BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) or Canadian provincial equivalent or Registered Nurse (RN) license number (if practicing outside Canada) Work Experience: minimum six months work experience in an acute care setting Submit a resume of work experience with your application. Exceptions may be granted for undergraduate students taking entry-level theory courses or new graduates. A resume is required for placement in the program. If you have questions about whether your work experience qualifies, please contact the program head. Interested nurses from international practice, residential, or other areas of care lacking recent (within two years) acute care experience may be required to complete a refresher course. BCIT recommends the following programs: Douglas College Kwantlen Polytechnic University Thompson Rivers University Please contact one of the institutions above, as well as the program head, to determine an appropriate preparatory course of study. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Clinical requirements Note: Effective immediately, all healthcare workers who come into contact with patients at publicly funded healthcare facilities or in the community, including at long-term care facilities, will have to get the influenza vaccine or wear a mask during flu season. This policy affects all students who will be entering a clinical setting. As such, you will be required to provide proof of your immunization or agree to wear a mask at all times prior to being placed in your clinical studies. Basic Cardiac Life Support Certification All students participating in clinical courses must have current Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), Level C or Level Health Care Provider (HCP). CPR certification must be from a Canadian provider and include a practical component. The original certificate must be presented upon application to clinical courses. BC College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) registration As well as providing this information at the time of admission, BCIT requires students to provide proof of BCCNM membership, Canadian provincial equivalent, or RN license number for each clinical course. Without proper registration, you will not be permitted to continue in the course. Face Respirator Fit Testing A face piece respiratory fit test is required before students are permitted to enter the clinical practicum. Upon successful completion of the fit test, the original certificate must be presented to the program and annual re-fitting is required. Students are expected to carry their certificate with them at all times during their practicum. For the Respirator Fit Testing, fit testing with a N95 respirator (1860, 1860s, or 1870) is required and must be performed, in accordance with CSA Standard CAN/CSA-Z94.4-02. Fit Testing must also include inspection, cleaning, maintenance, and storage of protective equipment. Students will be given specific instructions in preparation for their fit testing by the provider they choose. International applicants This program is available to international applicants who will complete the program from outside Canada or who currently have a valid work permit in Canada that will be valid for the duration of clinical training. Study permit: International applicants accepted into this program are not eligible for a study permit. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : While this program currently meets the study program - graduates with a bachelor’s degree criteria to apply for a PGWP, this program is not eligible for a PGWP due to other criteria not being met. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a bachelor’s degree. Apply to program International students must receive program head approval before applying. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply Prior Learning Assessment & Recognition (PLAR) The program faculty assesses learners with previous Specialty Nursing course work and relevant work experience on an individual basis. The program assesses learners with previous BCIT course work for potential credit into the degree program. The program may grant transfer of credit for non-BCIT Specialty courses. The program assesses experiential learning through prior learning assessment processes. The Registrar's office assesses transfer of credit for Liberal Studies courses. BCIT requires original, sealed transcripts and course outlines to assess transfer of credit. myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. Go back Overview Next up Costs & Supplies
